title: ImageResize removes EXIF data, with "Remove metadata" turned off
author: Hypano

status.label: Needs focused diagnostics
status.detail: Multiple users confirm the metadata regression, but a current PowerToys diagnostic archive and a safe before/after sample are still needed to isolate the failing metadata path.

next_action.label: Request current diagnostics
next_action.reason: Collect a fresh PowerToys bug report and representative metadata output immediately after reproducing.

judgment.rationale: The report already establishes a repeatable regression across multiple PowerToys versions and users. The new discussion concerns a third-party workaround and does not identify which Image Resizer metadata read/write path is dropping EXIF fields, so implementation work still needs current PowerToys diagnostics and a privacy-safe comparison of retained and removed tags.
evidence: The original report provides concrete Image Resizer settings and states that GPS, camera, and lighting metadata are removed even when metadata removal is disabled.
Multiple users reproduced the behavior, including on PowerToys 0.100.2, and reported that reverting to 0.98.1 restores the expected behavior.
The two September 1 comments discuss how to use an external workaround and add no new PowerToys diagnostic evidence.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask for a fresh /bugreport archive captured immediately after reproduction and a privacy-safe before/after EXIF tag comparison.

issue_context.summary: Image Resizer removes EXIF fields from rewritten JPEGs even though the metadata-removal option is disabled. Reports indicate a regression after 0.98.1 that remains reproducible on 0.100.2.
known_information: The reporter uses 100% dimensions, JPEG quality 70%, overwrite enabled, ignore orientation enabled, and metadata removal disabled.
Original and backup files retain the metadata while the transformed output loses at least GPS and camera/lighting fields.
Several users independently confirmed the behavior, and two users reported that 0.98.1 does not exhibit it.
The latest comments concern a third-party workaround rather than new PowerToys reproduction evidence.
inferences: The version comparison suggests a PowerToys Image Resizer regression introduced after 0.98.1, but the responsible metadata component is not yet confirmed.
A before/after tag comparison may distinguish wholesale metadata loss from selective omission by the image codec or metadata-copy stage.
issue_context.analysis: The reproduction settings and cross-user confirmations are sufficient to treat this as a credible bug, so repeating a generic reproduction checklist would not help. A fresh diagnostic archive can identify the current PowerToys and imaging-library path, while a sanitized tag comparison shows exactly which metadata classes survive the rewrite without requiring users to expose private photo contents or GPS values.
initial_investigation: The issue remains open with Product-Image Resizer and Needs-Triage labels.
Reports span PowerToys 0.99.1 through 0.100.2 and consistently identify 0.98.1 as a working version.
No PowerToys bug-report ZIP or machine-readable before/after metadata listing has been attached.

actions.label: Request current Image Resizer diagnostics

comment.body:
Thanks for the detailed settings and the confirmations across several PowerToys versions. The reports already show that resized JPEGs lose GPS and camera-related EXIF fields with metadata removal disabled, while 0.98.1 behaves correctly. The latest comments are about the external workaround, so we still need evidence from a current PowerToys run to isolate the failing metadata path.

Could someone reproduce this once on the latest stable or Preview build and then submit a comment containing `/bugreport` immediately afterward, attaching the generated ZIP? Please also share either a non-sensitive sample original/output pair or a privacy-safe list of EXIF tag names that are present before resizing and missing afterward. Please redact values such as coordinates and device serial numbers; tag names and presence/absence are sufficient.
